process_area.title: Weights & Measures Compliance, MRM & Measurement Analytics

fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, Compliance/Regulatory (links to VS-22), Quality (links to VS-31), Store/DC Operations, DTI-BPS Inspector/Authorized Verifier, Legal (links to VS-100.3)
fields.Trigger: Statutory verification cycle (W3625/W3626/W3629); DTI inspection; new legal-for-trade device
fields.Volume: Legal-for-trade measuring devices across 200 stores + 4 DCs

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Metrology Manager/Compliance maintain the legal-for-trade device register and" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "record in the register" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-inspect of "inspection response and findings" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: statutory calendar; operational: closure tracking
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unsealed-device risk**: Operating a commerce device without a valid DTI seal attracts penalty and consumer complaint; mitigated by statutory calendar
- **Inspection-finding risk**: DTI findings not remediated escalate; mitigated by closure tracking
System Touchpoints: - Device register (links to W3620); records (links to W3624); compliance (links to VS-22); legal (links to VS-100.3); audit (links to VS-21); analytics (links to W3640)

steps.activity: Metrology Manager/Compliance maintain the legal-for-trade device register and statutory calendar: every POS scale, catch-weight scale, and weighbridge used in commerce, the verification/seal expiry, the DTI RDO jurisdiction, and the authorized verifier; ensure all commerce devices are verified/sealed (Consumer Act RA 7394, Fair Trade Law)

Metrology Manager/Compliance coordinate statutory verification by DTI or an authorized verifier: schedule, witness/perform verification, secure the seal/sticker and certificate, record in the register (links to W3620/W3624), and manage re-verification on device change/move/repair; manage DTI inspections and findings

Metrology Manager/Compliance manage DTI inspection response and findings (links to VS-22/W77-style regulatory response): non-compliance (unsealed/expired device, tampered seal), corrective action, penalty management, and consumer-complaint defense; report DTI weights & measures compliance to governance (W3640) and audit (links to VS-21)

fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, Quality (links to VS-31), Device Owners (Stores/DC/Services), Finance (links to VS-17), Compliance (links to VS-22), Audit (links to VS-21), IT (links to VS-27)
fields.Trigger: OOT detected during calibration (W3622/W3625–W3632); customer/inventory discrepancy
fields.Volume: OOT events across the device estate

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Metrology Manager quarantine the OOT device" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "Metrology Manager investigate the OOT root cause" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document the OOT and correction" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-576 (ensure controlled execution — Weights & Measures Compliance, MRM & Measurement Analytics (PA-115.3).)
- operational: calibration cadence and variance monitoring (W3635); operational: impact-window analysis
Pain Points / Risks: - **Silent-OOT risk**: OOT device stays in service leaking revenue/causing errors; mitigated by calibration cadence and variance monitoring (W3635)
- **Under-correction risk**: OOT impact on past transactions not assessed/remediated; mitigated by impact-window analysis
System Touchpoints: - Device registry (links to W3620); records (links to W3624); AR/revenue (links to VS-16/VS-17); inventory (links to VS-05); quality (links to VS-31); analytics (links to W3635/W3640)

steps.activity: Metrology Manager quarantine the OOT device: remove from legal-for-trade/commerce service, label out-of-service, swap with a calibrated spare (links to W3636), and prevent further use until corrected; preserve as-found state and notify the device owner and quality

Metrology Manager investigate the OOT root cause: device failure, drift, damage, environmental, misuse, or standard error (links to W3618); assess the measurement impact window (since last-known-good calibration) and the population of affected transactions/records (revenue, inventory, quality acceptances links to W3635)

Metrology Manager/Finance manage the measurement correction: correct/recalibrate or repair the device (W3636), assess and process revenue/AR corrections for under/over-charge (links to VS-16/VS-17), inventory corrections (links to VS-05), and quality re-inspection; document the OOT and correction (W3624), and feed prevention to intervals/training/device design (W3619/W3623); report to governance (W3640)

fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, BI (links to VS-28.1), Finance/FP&A (links to VS-17.4), Quality (links to VS-31), Loss Prevention (links to VS-23), Store/DC Operations, ExCo (links to VS-33.2)
fields.Trigger: Monthly/quarterly analytics cycle; OOT (W3634); variance threshold

workflows.name: Measurement Variance, Revenue Impact & Loss Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Metrology Manager/BI instrument measurement-variance metrics" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-issue of "issue material/yield loss" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track reduction over time" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-576 (ensure controlled execution — Weights & Measures Compliance, MRM & Measurement Analytics (PA-115.3).)
- operational: variance analytics and impact modeling; operational: value-at-risk ranking
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hidden-leakage risk**: Revenue leakage from measurement drift hidden in margins; mitigated by variance analytics and impact modeling
- **Analytics-inaction risk**: Variance known but not prioritized; mitigated by value-at-risk ranking
System Touchpoints: - BI (links to VS-28.1); POS/transaction (links to VS-08); inventory (links to VS-05); finance (links to VS-17.4); LP (links to VS-23); analytics (links to W3640)

steps.activity: Metrology Manager/BI instrument measurement-variance metrics: scale-transaction variance (expected vs. actual weight/charge on catch-weight), cut-length variance/yield, paint-dose variance, weighbridge inbound/outbound variance, fuel variance (links to VS-61), and inventory-count variance attributable to measurement; identify outliers and drift

Metrology Manager/Finance quantify the revenue/cost impact: under-charge revenue leakage on catch-weight (POS scale reading low), over-issue material/yield loss (cutting/paint/dispensing), inventory inaccuracy cost (links to VS-05), and quality cost (false accept/reject); model the value-at-risk by device class

Metrology Manager publish the measurement-variance and impact analytics to executives (links to VS-33.2) and governance (W3640), feed high-impact devices to calibration priority and OOT investigation (W3634), and track reduction over time; coordinate with Loss Prevention on measurement-driven shrink (links to VS-23)

fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, Facilities (links to VS-20.3/VS-07.2), IT/ITAM (links to VS-27/VS-99), Procurement (links to VS-34), Finance (links to VS-35), Store/DC Operations, Vendor

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Metrology Manager/Facilities manage device lifecycle" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "track repair history per device" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-register of "Metrology Manager/Finance/Facilities manage device retirement" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-576 (ensure controlled execution — Weights & Measures Compliance, MRM & Measurement Analytics (PA-115.3).)
- operational: spare pool; operational: compliant disposal
Pain Points / Risks: - **Spare-shortage risk**: No calibrated spare causes downtime when a device fails; mitigated by spare pool
- **Improper-disposal risk**: E-waste/device disposal breaches environmental rules; mitigated by compliant disposal
System Touchpoints: - Procurement (links to VS-34); fixed asset (links to VS-35); ITAM/disposal (links to VS-99.1); facilities (links to VS-20.3/VS-07.2); e-waste (links to VS-73); device registry (links to W3620)

steps.activity: Metrology Manager/Facilities manage device lifecycle: specification/procurement of new devices (links to VS-34) with calibration/metrology requirements specified, incoming acceptance calibration, deployment with initial verification (W3633), and the in-service maintenance (links to VS-07.2/VS-20.3); maintain the spare-pool for swap

Metrology Manager/Vendor manage device repair: diagnose failure, in-house vs. vendor repair, post-repair calibration and re-verification (W3633) before return to service, and the repair cost/benefit vs. replace decision; track repair history per device

Metrology Manager/Finance/Facilities manage device retirement: end-of-life assessment, disposal (electronic-waste for digital devices links to VS-73/VS-99.1, secure data wipe for connected devices), asset retirement (links to VS-35), and removal from the register (W3620); refresh on the technology cycle

fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, Finance/FP&A (links to VS-17.4), Procurement (links to VS-34), Quality (links to VS-31), External Labs (W3621), BI (links to VS-28.1)
fields.Trigger: Annual budget cycle (links to VS-33.1); quarterly analytics; outsourcing review

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Metrology Manager/Finance capture the calibration program cost" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "discount, and self-service opportunities" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track cost-per-calibration and currency SLA over time, and feed optimization to…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-576 (ensure controlled execution — Weights & Measures Compliance, MRM & Measurement Analytics (PA-115.3).)
- operational: cost capture and allocation; operational: make-vs-buy analysis
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cost-opacity risk**: Calibration cost scattered and unmanaged; mitigated by cost capture and allocation
- **Sub-optimal-sourcing risk**: Defaulting to external when in-house is cheaper (or vice versa); mitigated by make-vs-buy analysis
System Touchpoints: - Finance (links to VS-17.4); procurement (links to VS-34); BI (links to VS-28.1); external labs (links to W3621); program strategy (links to W3617); analytics (links to W3640)

steps.activity: Metrology Manager/Finance capture the calibration program cost: in-house labor and standards, external lab fees (W3621), DTI verification fees (W3633), spare-pool, device depreciation, and OOT-impact cost (W3634/W3635); allocate to stores/DC/category

Metrology Manager/Procurement analyze the in-house vs. external sourcing mix: cost, turnaround, quality, and coverage by device class; identify consolidation, volume-discount, and self-service opportunities; manage the make-vs-buy decision per device class

Metrology Manager/Finance publish the calibration cost and service-level analytics to executives (links to VS-33.2) and governance (W3640), track cost-per-calibration and currency SLA over time, and feed optimization to the program strategy (W3617) and sourcing (W3621)

fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, Quality (links to VS-31), Calibration Technicians (W3622), Device Operators, Process Owners, Statistics/BI (links to VS-28)
fields.Trigger: New/critical measurement process; quality/acceptance concern; OOT trend
fields.Volume: Critical measurement systems (quality, acceptance, cut-length, dispensing)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "conduct Measurement System Analysis" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-measure of "measurement system contributes excessive variation, address device" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "integrate MSA into the quality/acceptance design" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-576 (ensure controlled execution — Weights & Measures Compliance, MRM & Measurement Analytics (PA-115.3).)
- operational: MSA and Gage R&R; operational: periodic re-validation
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unfit-measurement-system risk**: Measurement variation larger than tolerance produces wrong decisions; mitigated by MSA and Gage R&R
- **MSA-neglect risk**: MSA done once and never refreshed; mitigated by periodic re-validation
System Touchpoints: - Quality (links to VS-31); calibration (links to W3622); training (links to W3623); records (links to W3624); analytics (links to VS-28/W3640)

steps.activity: Metrology Manager/Quality conduct Measurement System Analysis (MSA) on critical measurement systems: bias, linearity, stability, and repeatability & reproducibility (Gage R&R — the variation from the measurement system vs. the process); identify whether the measurement system is fit for acceptance decisions (% study variation, ndc)

Metrology Manager/Quality act on MSA findings: if the measurement system contributes excessive variation, address device (calibration/repair W3634), method (procedure), operator (training W3623), environment, or standard; re-run MSA to confirm improvement

Metrology Manager integrate MSA into the quality/acceptance design (links to VS-31): ensure measurement systems underlying product acceptance, cut-length charge, and dispensing are validated for their decision; maintain MSA records (W3624) and report to governance (W3640) and quality audit (links to VS-31/VS-21)

fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, Customer Service (links to VS-13), Store/DC Operations, Quality (links to VS-31), Finance (links to VS-16/VS-17), Compliance (links to VS-22), Legal (links to VS-100)
fields.Trigger: Customer measurement dispute (catch-weight charge, cut-length, paint color, bulk quantity)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Metrology Manager receive and log the measurement dispute" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "verify the device calibration" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document, capture in dispute analytics" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-576 (ensure controlled execution — Weights & Measures Compliance, MRM & Measurement Analytics (PA-115.3).)
- operational: prompt investigation and resolution; operational: dispute analytics feeding OOT/correction
Pain Points / Risks: - **Dispute-escalation risk**: Unresolved measurement dispute escalates to DTI/consumer complaint; mitigated by prompt investigation and resolution
- **Repeat-dispute risk**: Recurring disputes from the same device/store; mitigated by dispute analytics feeding OOT/correction
System Touchpoints: - Customer service (links to VS-13); device registry/records (links to W3620/W3624); AR/refund (links to VS-16/VS-17); compliance (links to VS-22); analytics (links to W3640)

steps.activity: Customer Service/Metrology Manager receive and log the measurement dispute: transaction detail (catch-weight charge, cut length, paint color, bulk quantity), the device involved, the customer's claim, and evidence (receipt, sample, photo); acknowledge within SLA (links to VS-13.1)

Metrology Manager investigate the dispute: verify the device calibration status (W3620/W3624), re-measure/re-weigh the item if available, assess whether the device was OOT (W3634), and determine validity; coordinate with the store/quality and the customer

Metrology Manager/Customer Service/Finance resolve the dispute: refund/adjustment for valid under/over-charge (links to VS-16/VS-17/W101), good-will gesture, and corrective action if device OOT (W3634); document, capture in dispute analytics (W3640), and feed prevention; manage escalation to DTI/consumer complaint if unresolved (links to VS-22)
steps.r: Metrology Manager / Customer Service / Finance / Legal

fields.Participants: Metrology Manager, Quality (links to VS-31), Audit (links to VS-21), Innovation (links to VS-30), IT (links to VS-27), Finance (links to VS-17.4), ExCo (links to VS-33.2), Compliance (links to VS-22)
fields.Trigger: Annual cycle; strategy refresh (W3617); audit; technology opportunity

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "assess metrology maturity" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-report of "identify improvements and innovation" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-576 (ensure controlled execution — Weights & Measures Compliance, MRM & Measurement Analytics (PA-115.3).)
- operational: innovation and connected/predictive approaches; operational: independent audit input
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stagnation risk**: Program never advances beyond manual calendar-based calibration; mitigated by innovation and connected/predictive approaches
- **Self-assessment bias risk**: Maturity overstated; mitigated by independent audit input
System Touchpoints: - Audit (links to VS-21); innovation (links to VS-30); IT/IoT (links to VS-27); analytics (links to VS-28/W3635); PMO (links to VS-112); strategy (links to W3617); ExCo (links to VS-33.2)

steps.activity: Metrology Manager/Audit assess metrology maturity: program governance (W3617), traceability integrity (W3618), interval optimization (W3619), registry completeness (W3620), calibration currency/OOT rate (W3622/W3634), MSA coverage (W3638), regulatory compliance (W3633), cost-effectiveness (W3637), and analytics maturity (W3635); benchmark to good practice

Metrology Manager identify improvements and innovation: automated/connected calibration (IoT-connected scales self-reporting drift), digital calibration certificates, predictive calibration (usage/condition-based), self-service store calibration for simple devices, and measurement-analytics integration (links to VS-28/VS-30); prioritize and resource via the PMO (links to VS-112)

Metrology Manager report metrology maturity, improvement progress, and value to ExCo (links to VS-33.2) and governance, and feed learnings to program strategy (W3617), standards (W3618), intervals (W3619), and training (W3623); drive continuous improvement
